attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in a numbered list headed as what he actually thinks. Not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: Present-tense, unhedged statement about LLMs as of Dec 2024. Paraphrasing 'not remotely' as 'not come close' is faithful. It has no conditions or horizon. Context shows he still credits LLMs with real uses in writing and coding.

contract.note: Marcus did not name the promises, who made them, what counts as initial, or a standard for 'remotely'. The contract fairly declines to choose a baseline for him, since any choice would decide the verdict. It does not set out a plain reading to score.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own March 2023 product announcement, dated before the post. It is one company's capability statement. It cannot show which promises Marcus meant or whether LLMs fell far short of them overall.

reviews.rationale: The claim is firm but has no identifiable baseline: the 'initial promises' and the standard for falling 'remotely' short are unspecified. Scoring it would need a set of promises picked by the evaluator, and that pick would decide the result. The only evidence item is a single company disclosure, which is context only. The claim is too vague to score; the case itself is not broken.
